Multimodal QuantTree (MMQT)

Source: R/dfr_mmqt.R
mmqt.Rd

Batch-wise change detector for stationary conditions made of several modalities (Stucchi et al., 2023). Every stationary batch is drawn from one of a set of unknown distributions, for instance the operating modes of a machine, and a change is any batch that comes from none of them. MMQT builds a single QuantTree histogram over the training batches, clusters their bin-probability vectors to find the modalities, and tests each new batch against the modality closest to it with a modality-specific threshold that controls the false positive rate.

Usage

mmqt(
  training,
  nu = NULL,
  bins = 16,
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_modalities = NULL,
  alpha_modalities = 0.05,
  max_modalities = 10,
  calibration = TRUE,
  n_repeats = 10,
  n_sim = 10000,
  partition = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

training

The training set: a list of batches (matrices or data frames with the same columns and nu rows each), or a single matrix or data frame that is cut into consecutive batches of nu rows (an incomplete last batch is dropped).

nu

Number of observations per batch. Taken from the batches when training is a list.

bins

Number of bins K of the histogram, built with uniform target probabilities 1 / K.

alpha

Target false positive rate of the test.

n_modalities

Number of modalities M. NULL (the default) estimates it with Algorithm 1 of the paper: the smallest M whose detector has an empirical false positive rate on the training batches not above alpha_modalities.

alpha_modalities

Target false positive rate alpha' used to estimate the number of modalities.

max_modalities

Largest number of modalities tried by the estimation.

calibration

Whether to calibrate the bin probabilities of each modality (Eqs. 12-13), which corrects for a histogram built on the data of all modalities.

n_repeats

Number of times the estimation is repeated, each with a new histogram. The number of modalities is the most frequent estimate, and the histogram the one whose training false positive rate is closest to alpha_modalities among those that gave it. Ignored when n_modalities is given.

n_sim

Number of Monte Carlo simulations used to compute each threshold.

partition

A partitioning from another mmqt model (model$partition) to reuse instead of building a new one.

seed

Seed of a private random number stream, so that training does not change the global one. NULL uses the global generator.

Value

An mmqt object with the partitioning (partition), the reference bin probabilities of each modality (reference, one row per modality), their thresholds (thresholds), the number of training batches of each modality (n_batches), the false positive rate on the training batches (training_fpr) and, when the number of modalities was estimated, the estimates of every repetition (estimation).

Details

Histogram. The partitioning is a QuantTree (Boracchi et al., 2018), ported from the reference code: each bin is cut from the remaining space along a random coordinate, at the sample quantile that leaves the target share of the remaining training points in the bin. Its bin probabilities have a distribution that does not depend on the data, so the threshold of the total variation statistic T = 0.5 * sum(|p - pi|) can be computed by simulation for any data (Frittoli et al., 2022): the bin probabilities of the histogram are drawn from their Dirichlet distribution and the counts of a batch from a multinomial, n_sim times, and the threshold is the 1 - alpha quantile of the simulated statistic.

Modalities. The bin-probability vectors of the training batches are clustered by k-means (k-means++ initialization, ten starts). The centroid of a cluster estimates the bin probabilities pi^m of a modality, which are calibrated as in Eq. 12, and the modality gets the threshold of a QuantTree with probabilities pi^m built on the nu N_m points of its N_m batches.

Monitoring. A batch is assigned to the modality whose (calibrated) bin probabilities are closest in Euclidean distance (Eq. 7), and a change is detected when its statistic against that modality exceeds the modality's threshold (Eqs. 8-9).

The calibration needs, for every bin, the training points of the modality closest to the bin boundary inside and outside the bin. When the modality has no point on one of the two sides, g is set to 0.

The reference repository (https://github.com/diegocarrera89/quantTree) implements QuantTree, but its MMQT is announced as "coming soon"; MMQT is therefore implemented from the paper.

References

Stucchi, D., Magri, L., Carrera, D. and Boracchi, G. (2023). Multimodal batch-wise change detection. IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 34(10), 6783-6797. doi:10.1109/TNNLS.2023.3294846

Boracchi, G., Carrera, D., Cervellera, C. and Maccio, D. (2018). QuantTree: histograms for change detection in multivariate data streams. Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 639-648.

See also

mmqt_test() to test batches and dfr_mmqt() to monitor a stream.

Examples

# Two operating modes; a change moves the first one.
set.seed(1)
mode <- function(n, center) matrix(stats::rnorm(2 * n, center), ncol = 2)
training <- c(lapply(1:20, function(i) mode(64, 0)), lapply(1:20, function(i) mode(64, 4)))
model <- mmqt(training, bins = 8, n_repeats = 2, n_sim = 2000, seed = 1)
model$n_modalities
#> [1] 2
mmqt_test(model, list(mode(64, 0), mode(64, 4), mode(64, 1.5)))
#>   modality  statistic threshold drift
#> 1        2 0.06758636 0.1603606 FALSE
#> 2        1 0.03124695 0.1604548 FALSE
#> 3        2 0.62441452 0.1603606  TRUE
